They share the specific topic of identifying the primary business drivers for segment financial performance.

current_disclosures.section: Results of Operations > Operating Income by Reportable Segments
current_disclosures.summary: Compute & Networking revenue increased year-over-year due to strong demand for accelerated computing and AI solutions. Data Center computing revenue grew 162% driven by the Hopper computing platform for large language models and generative AI, while Data Center networking revenue grew 51% driven by Ethernet for AI and the Spectrum-X end-to-end ethernet platform.

materiality_analysis.reason: The 2025 disclosure explicitly identifies Spectrum-X as a specific driver of the 51% growth in Data Center networking revenue, whereas the 2024 disclosure only announced its introduction. This represents a material update to the company's business performance, confirming the commercial adoption and financial impact of this specific strategic product platform.

comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD report significant double-digit growth in their primary high-growth Data Center segments driven by AI workloads. NVDA attributes its 266% Compute growth and 133% Networking growth to higher shipments of Hopper GPUs for LLMs and InfiniBand. Similarly, AMD reports a 94% increase in Data Center net revenue, driven by higher sales of Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs. While both companies cite AI accelerator sales as the primary growth driver, NVDA discloses specific product architecture (Hopper) and networking technology (InfiniBand) drivers with larger percentage growth rates compared to AMD's broader attribution to Instinct and EPYC product lines.

sentences.text: Compute grew 266% due to higher shipments of the NVIDIA Hopper GPU computing platform for the training and inference of LLMs, recommendation engines and generative AI applications.
Networking was up 133% due to higher shipments of InfiniBand.
Data Center net revenue of $12.6 billion in 2024 increased by 94%, compared to net revenue of $6.5 billion in 2023.
The increase was primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs.
